input.quote: Such audit shall not occur more than [***] in a given Calendar Year, unless for cause, and shall not concern books and records relating to a period more than [***] preceding the current Calendar Year.
input.rationale: Section 9.9 is the only audit right that binds us on payments/records (Section 6.9 runs in our favour, auditing RevMed and its subcontractors). It contains every material protection the playbook seeks: a mutual and reciprocal right, a fixed minimum prior-notice period, a per-Calendar-Year frequency cap, a defined look-back with waiver of older periods, an independent auditor of international prominence subject to our reasonable acceptance, scope limited to verifying financial reports and payments, an express bar on disclosing our Confidential Information to RevMed beyond the discrepancy report (9.9(b)), and cost borne by the auditing Party unless an underpayment exceeds a stated percentage threshold (9.9(c)). There is no right of remote or direct access to our systems — the auditor reviews books and records only — so the walk-away scenario does not arise. Two minor points are noted rather than flagged: the notice period, frequency, look-back and underpayment percentage are redacted as [***], so they cannot be confirmed against the preferred 30 days / once per 12 months / 5% (or the fallback 15 days / 10%) figures; and the "unless for cause" carve-out to the frequency cap is a customary exception rather than an unlimited-audit right. Overall the clause sits at or above the fallback on its material terms, so no redline is warranted.
